title: Hazel as an npm Package: What to Decide Next
blurb: Where the hazeljs package stands at 0.0.11, for Matthew and Cyrus: one PR (#2857) that it is built from, how that branch differs from dev, and every game in hazeljs-examples timed four ways. The package's jit runs the games 317× as fast as its interpreter (geometric mean over 45 operations), from 4.2× to 4,955×: on searches it is as fast as code compiled ahead of time, but on light calls with a large state most of its time goes to converting values in and out. Compiled ahead of time, the games run 2,392× as fast as interpreted, and the five written by hand in JavaScript about 16× faster again. A day later, with #2857's converters by declared type, the jit ran them 9.0× as fast again on the benchmark's repeated positions; on each game's own run of states it takes 0.91 of the time of code compiled ahead of time, and 0.76 with the converters' memos kept as links on the objects rather than in WeakMaps (build 6); 2.2 times its own when every state is a fresh copy. Then the decisions before it merges into dev.
